A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same SDTrack study, with matching methods and experiments. Neither contains appendices or the Supplementary Materials referenced in the text; those unavailable materials cannot be compared.

before.justification: v2 reports original SDTrack evaluations on FE108, FELT, and VisEvent, together with architecture ablations, sensitivity experiments, and qualitative tracking examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original SDTrack benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity experiments, and qualitative tracking examples in Sections 4–5.

M1.justification: GTP, IPL, the backbone, training losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Both versions already specify floating-point final head convolutions. Reordering Equations 13–15 and generalizing the neuron description do not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K pretraining and evaluate event-based tracking on FE108, FELT, and VisEvent. The degraded-condition examples also remain; no dataset, task, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Removing v2 Table 4 removes the dedicated comparison against the fully spike-driven tracking-head variant. The external tracker set in Table 1 and candidate backbone set in Table 3 remain unchanged; Spike-driven V1–V3 are merely abbreviated to SDT V1–V3.

E3.justification: The retained experiments report the same model configurations, time steps, input resolutions, training scheme, evaluation metrics, and energy-estimation assumptions. No revised splits, training budgets, or testing procedures are documented.

E4.justification: v3 removes Table 4 and its analysis of adding a neuronal layer before the final head convolution, eliminating a direct accuracy-versus-energy ablation. The IPL, positional encoding, head-type, pretraining, backbone, and GTP sensitivity analyses remain, as do the qualitative degraded-condition examples.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The revised plots do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical numerical results. v3 removes Table 4's AUC/PR/energy results: 59.0/91.3/7.9967 mJ for SDTrack Head versus 58.9/90.4/7.9963 mJ for Spike-driven Head. It also omits the 43.2-to-19.7 AUC drop in v2's ODTrack-failure paragraph, whose model attribution is internally inconsistent because one sentence names SDTrack.

T1.justification: The supplied mathematical content remains equivalent: neuron parameters are renamed and Equations 13–15 are reordered without changing their dependencies. Neither PDF includes the referenced supplementary derivation, so no change to that unavailable proof can be established.

C1.justification: The introduction drops repeated claims that the tracker, operations, and head are fully spike-driven, qualifying the claim consistently with the floating-point layers already disclosed in v2. The principal novelty, GTP/IPL contributions, performance, and efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds an interpretation that GTP's temporal channel helps recover texture-related information. Section 5 replaces the single-token explanation of ODTrack incompatibility with temporal-feature confusion and removes the general LIF coordinate-prediction caveat and the final convolution's negligible-energy explanation. Section 3.3 also softens the localization deficiency from impossible to difficult to compensate through learning.

D1.justification: v3 adds an abstract link stating that code and models are available, whereas v2 only promises a release; v3 nevertheless retains that future-release wording in Section 4.1. Conversely, Figure 6's caption no longer states that the alpha sweep used two-channel event images. The principal implementation and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 removes four cited works: Xception, DashNet, Wang et al.'s high-resolution event-tracking benchmark, and Zhang et al.'s frame-event alignment and fusion network. The central positioning relative to event aggregation methods, hybrid SNN trackers, and spike-driven Transformers remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites parts of the neuron and GTP explanations, condenses the discussion and conclusion, adjusts headings, and edits the author and affiliation list. These are localized revisions within substantially the same document structure.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is adjusted, Figures 4–5 receive plotting and labeling changes, and Figure 6 combines its two sensitivity panels into one plot with separate horizontal scales. Table 2 moves, Table 4 disappears, and surrounding content reflows; the retained displays largely present the same evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 usefully qualifies the fully spike-driven claim and supplies code/model access information. However, it removes the direct empirical test of the final head convolution's accuracy/energy tradeoff while retaining its necessity claim, and makes the ODTrack limitation less quantitative. With the main results unchanged and no replacement evidence supplied, these losses modestly weaken evidential support and transparency.
